title_html: Partner selection, due diligence & term sheet—before any filing.

items_html: Before any filing, identify the Chinese partner and run corporate, credit, litigation, and licence checks—not a shell holding the wrong assets.
Sign a non-binding term sheet or LOI covering equity split, governance intent, capital schedule, and exclusivity.
Typical timeline: 4–8 weeks (longer for SOE or multi-party deals).
Most JV failures trace to the wrong partner, not registration errors—budget counsel and DD separately from incorporation agents.

title_html: Negotiate the JV / shareholder agreement and Articles of Association (章程).

items_html: Under the Foreign Investment Law and 2024 Company Law, new JVs are standard limited liability companies—the old EJV/CJV statutes no longer govern new formations.
The shareholder agreement is private; the Articles are filed with AMR. Governance, deadlock, IP, ROFR/tag-drag, and profit policy belong here.
Typical timeline: 4–8 weeks—often the longest pre-filing step.
Post-2020 law: the shareholders' meeting is the supreme organ—not the board as under legacy EJV rules.

title_html: Map business scope against the 2024 National Negative List and obtain sector pre-approvals where required.

items_html: Off-list sectors follow domestic rules (内外资一致). On-list sectors require a Chinese co-investor at the mandated ownership level.
Most JVs submit a foreign-investment initial report with AMR registration—not a separate MOFCOM approval certificate.
Restricted sectors may need NDRC project filing/approval or MIIT/CAAC/MOF sector licences before or with registration.
Timeline: 0–24+ weeks—0 for unrestricted services; +2–6 months if sector approval is required.

title_html: Reserve the company name via AMR self-declaration (名称自主申报).

detail.html: Four-part format: administrative division + trade name + industry + org form. FIE names follow foreign-investor rules; retention is typically ~2 months. Names containing "China" or "(中国)" face stricter rules—agent pre-check recommended. Typical review: 1–5 working days.

title_html: Secure a commercial registered address and legalize foreign investor documents.

items_html: Commercial lease + landlord property ownership certificate (residential addresses are generally rejected for trading/manufacturing JVs).
Foreign corporate investors: notarize and apostille parent documents; individuals: apostille passports. Certified Chinese translations required.
Chinese partner provides domestic registration materials; align document dates with AMR filing—stale certificates get rejected.
Overseas apostille often gates the schedule—plan 2–4 weeks for this step.

title_html: File AMR establishment registration with foreign-investment initial report → receive Business License.

items_html: Submit establishment package: signed Articles, lease, all investor qualification packs, director/supervisor/legal rep appointments, and FDI initial report fields via the enterprise registration system.
Set subscribed registered capital and a 5-year pay-in schedule per 2024 Company Law Art. 47 in the Articles.
Typical review: 5–10 working days in many cities for unrestricted sectors when materials are complete.
No statutory minimum for most LLCs since 2014—but industry licences, customs, and banks impose practical floors.

title_html: Carve and file company chops (公章, 财务章, 法人章—invoice chop usually not needed under nationwide 数电票)—agree custody in the JV agreement first.

detail.html: PSB-filing seal vendor after licence. JV disputes often involve chop access—lock dual-sign and custody policies before the first chop is used. Some cities push electronic seals or offer free first sets for new market entrants. Typical: 3–7 working days.

title_html: Complete new-taxpayer information confirmation (多证合一) and enable fully digital electronic invoicing (数电发票).

detail.html: Often synchronized with AMR multi-certificate integration. Register for VAT/CIT as applicable. Both shareholders should align on transfer-pricing documentation early if related-party trading is expected. Typical: 1–2 weeks.

title_html: Open RMB basic and foreign-currency capital accounts; complete FDI FX registration at the bank.

items_html: Receive the business registration voucher (业务登记凭证) under SAFE's 2024 Capital Account FX Guidance—the gateway for inbound equity.
Legal representative in-person KYC is commonly required; bank choice matters for outbound payments and FX conversion.
Do not wire "registered capital" before accounts and FDI registration are ready—often the critical-path step (4–8 weeks).

title_html: Make capital contributions per the subscribed schedule (认缴制; no government验资 report for standard LLCs).

items_html: Foreign investors remit foreign currency to the capital account; Chinese investors contribute RMB or in-kind per appraisal rules.
In-kind / IP contributions must be valued by a qualified Chinese appraiser before AMR will accept them.
AMR publishes subscribed/paid amounts via the enterprise credit publicity system; first tranche often 1–2 weeks after accounts are ready.

title_html: Register for social insurance and housing fund before hiring.

detail.html: Employer contributions are separate from registered capital and paid from operating cash in the RMB basic account. Model payroll in your city tier on the dashboard before hiring. Typical: 1–2 weeks.

title_html: Obtain post-licensing permits: customs, ICP, and sector licences where applicable.

items_html: If importing/exporting, register with customs (海关注册)—separate from the AMR licence.
Internet platforms need ICP filing or licence; telecom VATS, education, medical, and broadcasting sectors need regulator permits—often the real timeline driver.
Technology import contracts may require MOFCOM registration/record-filing—budget legal review.
Annual foreign-investment report due 1 Jan–30 Jun via the enterprise credit system (starting year 2). Timeline: 2 weeks–6+ months, sector-dependent.
